items.title: Who wore it better? - Political Propaganda in the Buckeye State
items.text:
# Ground Zero

I live in a very purple county in a very purple state. What's that translate to in day to day living? Sooooooo much mail. I would like to share one piece of recent mail that made me laugh from each side of an election. Presumably, they may make you laugh as well.

# The Grand ol' Party

Representing the right side of the aisle, we have an ad that I find kind of silly. It **looks** like propaganda. What's probably most disturbing to me about this is that I can't actually figure out if it's supposed to be silly or not.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163714)

Then I turned it over. This drives me bonkers, and it's increasingly becoming common among political folk. Of course, I'm talking about using an adjective as a noun. "Illegals" cannot be plural because illegal cannot be singular. In the English, you can have illegal cucumber**s** or protractor**s** or even planet**s**, but you can't have illegal**s**.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163723)

It's just nonsensical. The only thing it says to a guy like me, is that the writer doesn't really have a strong handle on the English language, which is ironic, given what I think he's trying to express! A fun follow up question someone should have asked when proofreading this add is whether or not the writer was referring to legal illegals or illegal illegals. I think at that point, he could have clarified that he meant criminals.

# The Eeyores

Let's step to the left and see what's being distributed. To me this one is less fun and games, and far more sinister. My wife literally opened this up and started reading it to the family because it was from the "Center for Voter Information" and clearly looked like it was just listing where candidates stood on the issues. At first it worked. I still haven't heard any convincing reason to keep the Epstein files secret, and I didn't know where these two politicians stood on the issue. But before even reading the second question out loud, the Mrs. stopped, knowing that we were dealing with obvious propaganda.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163715)

I know that there are senators who want to keep the Epstein files secret, despite public sentiment. I've **never** heard a senator say they want to increase the debt to benefit billionaires. That's just not what any senator is going to say they are all about. This one doesn't **look** like propaganda, because it so obviously **is** propaganda.

But then again, is it all that obvious? Do people actually fall for this stuff? Are there really people in my neighborhood that dumb? I just can't believe it. Also, who wore it better? Do you guys think clumsy and goofy or sinister and disguised makes for more entertaining political theater.

items.title: Spaces Protocol Explained: Human-Readable Names on Bitcoin🧐
items.text:
Spaces Protocol provides human-readable names that replace long alphanumeric Bitcoin addresses. A user who owns a name can publish a Bitcoin address, a silent payment address, a Lightning offer, or any other payment records behind that name.


Senders resolve the name and receive the current payment instruction without copying a long string.


The same name can also serve as a Nostr username. 


Once the name is registered, the owner controls the records that appear when the name is looked up. The records can be updated later without changing the name itself.


Registration occurs through open auctions on the Bitcoin blockchain. The highest bidder at the close of the auction window becomes the owner of the top-level space. Bids are burned, so no central party retains the proceeds. The protocol limits new top-level spaces to roughly 3,600 per year, with up to ten advancing each day based on bid amount. 


After the claim period ends, the winning bidder controls the associated UTXO. 


That control can later be used to issue handles underneath the space. Handles such as alice@bitcoin are recorded in a Merkle tree. The operator commits the root of the tree to Bitcoin as a 32-byte hash. 


Each handle owner then receives a certificate that proves inclusion and prior non-existence. After the commitment confirms, the handle cannot be revoked by the operator or by any third party.


Verification of ownership does not require trust in a remote server for the final proof. 


A client can check the certificate against the Bitcoin-anchored root.


The design keeps most data off-chain while anchoring the commitment to Bitcoin’s proof of work. The on-chain footprint remains small because many handles share a single root. Handles do not expire and do not require annual renewal fees. 


Ownership rests with the private key that controls the certificate or the associated UTXO.


The protocol also supports the publication of records that point to content. 


A name can resolve to the location of a site or other data that is stored in a decentralized network rather than on a single server controlled by one operator. 


Traditional websites can be taken offline by the entity that operates the server or by an authority that directs that entity. Content referenced through a Spaces name remains reachable as long as the underlying network continues to host it and the name continues to resolve. 


The name itself is protected by the same Bitcoin security that secures ordinary transactions. No single party can seize the name once the claim has confirmed and the keys remain under the owner’s control.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163758)

Full Article: https://bitbane.com/bitcoin-spaces-protocol-explained-human-readable-names-on-bitcoin/

items.title: Austin trip day two: I ask to pay with bitcoin and someone tried to choke me
items.text:
Hey stackers,

Writing from the poker room after a four hour session. Taking a long break before I head back. Here’s my favorite hand from the sesh if you’re interested:

https://stacker.news/items/1603097/r/SatAttack?commentId=1603670

I woke up later than I wanted to knocking on my hotel door. It was 930 and housekeeping wanted to clean my room. I politely declined, got out of bed, brushed my teeth and quickly made my way out. There were things to see and bitcoin to spend. @plebpoet had recommended Caffe Medici as a place you can buy coffee and pastries for sats so that’s where I went first. There’s three locations and with some poking around I found the origional one. It’s in a nice quiet part of town and the ambience from outside looked really cool.

Here’s their BTCmap: [https://btcmap.org/merchant/way:382559089](https://btcmap.org/merchant/way:382559089)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163624)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163625)

I loved these stone chairs and tables. I wish I could have captured them all but some were being used and I didn’t want to take pictures of strangers. Inside was really nice too. Lots of plants and plenty of seating. I head to the counter where I see their square terminal and order a red eye which if you don’t know is an espresso shot with a regular coffee poured over it. It will clear the mind and wake up the bowels. Good for the morning. Right in the middle of asking if she would accept bitcoin she rings me up and answers my question; I see that wonderful toggle in the top left of some square terminals. I toggle to Bitcoin and I’m presented with a lightning address. I pay it with Phoenix no issues.

I asked her how often people pay with bitcoin—not very often, I guessed. She said only some times. She had been working there for four months and I was the third person to pay with sats. Not bad actually, I thought. It’s not like she rings everyone up, so there could have been others.

After a few sips of coffee and a couple pages from the second book of the Outlander series by Diana Gabaldon, I realized I had forgotten to check the parties! Fool boy. I asked where they came from, I don’t remember the name, but they get them from a local bakery here in Austin. I ended up with a blueberry muffin and toggled over to Bitcoin and sent another successful transaction.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163627)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163628)

I had plans to go to jiujitsu at the Austin 10th planet at 11 but waking up late was really deterring me from executing that plan. I really wanted to skip the workout and stay on this couch with my book and coffee. I read and read some more and checked the time. It was 1030. The gym was only 15 min away. There was time to not skip…. Over to my left I notice they have whole beans for sale on the shelf and decide there. I’ll
Buy some beans and stop being lazy. After the third lightning transaction in the last hour she tells me you get a free coffee with a bag of beans purchase….. UuuUgh it really sounded nice to sit and read with my free cup. Instead I take it to go and head to the gym.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163629)

I arrive at the gym 10 minutes before class time. I didnt bring a rash guard so I needed to buy one and told the guy over the counter as much. I asked if I could pay for both with bitcoin and he was a bit hesitant. “I think so” he said. He’s showing me the options for rash guards that are hanging on the racks when I see a box on the floor with some orange and black material inside. The box is labeled “b-coin”

Are these rash guards?! I ask
Oh yeah, they are. You want one of those?
Uuuuh YEAH. He pulls one out and shows it to me and it’s AWESOME. Here it is on me:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163630)

He had to text the owner and inquire about my bitcoin request. She responded pretty quickly and texted him a QR code made by cash app. The ones that you can pay either lightning or on-chain to. I took the opportunity to save some liquidity from my Phoenix channel and paid on-chain with Blue Wallet. I told him he should let her know I made an on-chain payment and that I was confident she’d be ok with that. And that she should receive the payment in about ten minutes. I paid 3sats/vB to ensure that was accurate.

Equipped with my new sweet rash guard it was time to start class. Everyone was very welcoming in introductions and we got to work pretty quickly. We warmed up with some bridges and shrimps and got right into the lesson. Today we were going to work on getting a hip toss from full guard and failing the attempt some attacks you can do instead.

My partner was great, I wish I remembered his name. I’m fairly novice, and he was patient and helped me with some important details on the attacks we were learning. We went over locking the Americana after the failed hip toss, then the guillotine, the triangle, the kimura, and omaplata all stemming from the original hip sweep attempt from full guard. during practice  I took a nasty elbow to the lip that swelled right away and filled my mouth with an iron taste (wear a mouthguard kids). Lesson complete, the next hour was open mat. They started the 5 min repeat clock and let people get sparring rounds in. I did a couple before hit hitting the showers. I’m a bit out of jiujitsu shape haha. Awesome stuff. Awesome class. Thanks coach Curtis!

![](https://m.stacker.news/163631)

On my way out the gym coach Curtis was at the front desk. I had asked him earlier for this group picture and told him I will
Blog about my day today on a forum. “Blog or vlog?” He asked.

Blog.

“People still read?” Haha YES I told him. And I told him where I’d blog as well I told him about stacker news and what it’s like. I told him the idea that because valuable things are used to express like-ness valuable content surfaces to the top. I showed him my stacker news and made a couple zaps. He was really intrigued. “A negligible amount I assume, like a small amount of sats?” Ummmm YES SIR. I was happy to hear him use the word sats. Bitcoin was normal for him, it seemed. He said he will check it out and that seemed like the perfect opportunity to give him one of the SN stickers @k00b gave me yesterday. He loved the sticker and joked about putting it up on the stall door so people were forced to see it. I’m sure he was joking but I really hope that happens. Then he asked me if I was the guy who paid with bitcoin today. I said yes and he goes “ok let me hook you up” (!!!)

He said anyone repping and using bitcoin he wants to help out. Wow… awesome. He starts digging around in the “b-coin” bin looking for a pair of shorts to give me. They didn’t have my size, unfortunately, and so he offered a long sleeve rash guard instead. I had to decline. I have many rash guards back at home and I didn’t want to take one just because it was free. He told me I can come back to the gym for free while I was on my trip… I was so grateful. How cool! He showed me around the gyms grocery store which was actually rather stocked. They had grass fed beef. They order by the cow and sell frozen beef from the gym. They had raw milks and other treats. Loaves of bread. All sorts of locally made goods. He told me the raw milks were made by a lady who loves bitcoin and sometimes they use Bitcoin to transact with her. Hooter Flats was the name of her company. I bought one of the chocolate milks. Perfect post-training snack.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163632)

Workout complete I wanted to head to play some poker but I needed to eat first. I pretty quickly decided to head back to the Green Mestique from yesterday and get the same thing but different meats. I ordered the turkey, chopped beef, and the sausage. I had to get that sausage again. For sides I got potato salad and repeated the green beans as well. When they brought my plate they had given me chicken  instead of the turkey. No matter, I knew it was great. I couldn’t resist putting the BBQ sauce all over the chicken even though it stung like hell the cut on my inner lip. But I worked through the tears and finished strong.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163634)

And that’s day two! I went to the poker room after this and I am just now starting another session. I’ll probably play a couple hours before heading to bed.

If you missed my day one report check it out here: https://stacker.news/items/1602995/r/SatAttack

See you stackers, thanks for reading.

One of the peace-of-mind ways to Spend from a Cold Wallet: PSBT
items.text:
With so many hacks in recent months, it got me thinking about a less risky way to spend from a cold wallet when the time comes (*I am not talking about daily spending, which is better with an LN wallet*).

Entering the seeds into ANY hot wallet became quite nerve-racking, what if the hot wallet got hacked? So I did some reading and digging, it turns out there is actually a way to solve this problem: PSBT (partially signed Bitcoin transaction) The logic is that you **sign the transaction offline, then broadcast it online**; this way, the seeds always stay offline!

During my experiment, interestingly, you *can't* sign transactions from a completely offline wallet because the balance needs to be synced first; However, you can do this from a watch-only wallet.

`This tutorial uses Blue Wallet with Electrum wallet as an example.`

1. Select the watch-only wallet, which is shown in gray in Blue Wallet.
   Hit "Send," enter the recipient address and the amount of btc; Tap "Next," then Export to file or Copy to Clipboard, now a partially signed transaction is created!

![](https://m.stacker.news/163681)

*Use any way you prefer to transfer this text or file to your offline machine.*

2. Open the Electrum wallet, **offline**.
   Go to tools - Load Transaction - Form Text / File - Load Transaction - `Sign`.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163682)

Go to left corner - click Share - Save to file or Copy to clipboard.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163683)

*Use any way you prefer to transfer this text or file to your online machine.*

3. Paste the Hex and use this tool [https://mempool.space/tx/push](https://mempool.space/tx/push) to broadcast the transaction and wait for it to be confirmed!

![](https://m.stacker.news/163679)

There we go. I think this is a quiet peace-of-mind way to spend from a cold wallet when the time comes, without needing to enter the seeds online. Have you tried this? Or have you found an even better way to spend from cold wallets? Feel free to share in the comments.

And I have a question in mind after trying this out: what if I signed the transaction, let's say today, would it ever expire? Like, can I broadcast it next week, next year, or even later? 🤔
